questions.question: What is the ANTONYM of the word ‘perfect’, as used in the passage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. **"Unsatisfactory".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Perfect**: (उत्तम) - Having all the required or desirable elements, qualities, or characteristics; as good as it is possible to be.

 
 
• **Example**: She strived to achieve a perfect score on her exam.
 
 
 
• **Unsatisfactory**: (असंतोषजनक) - Not satisfactory; not good enough.
 
 
• **Example**: The project was delayed due to unsatisfactory work by the contractor.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troublesome**: (कष्टप्रद) - Causing difficulty or annoyance. 
 
• **Limited**: (सीमित) - Restricted in size, amount, or extent; few, small, or short.
 
• **Laughable**: (हास्यास्पद) - So ludicrous as to be amusing.

questions.question: **According to the passage, animals in zoos suffer cruelty: **

options.text: by being kept in artificial environments
by being physically tortured or abused
by being forced to perform for the visitors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**by being kept in artificial environments**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fourth sentence of the first paragraph says "***Most animals are put in an artificial environment** (e.g., cages)*" and the fifth sentence of the first paragraph says "***This isolation** from their natural habitat **can amount to cruelty***".
 
• From the above sentences, we can say that according to the passage, animals in zoos suffer cruelty by being kept in artificial environments.

 

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ​Given below are the points, we should keep in mind while solving questions of reading comprehension-
 
 
• Identify the purpose of reading. Try to go through the question first then the passage so that you can just focus on the things you need to look in the passage.
 
• Anticipate what may lie ahead. Look out for specific information in the passage.
 
• Read the passage quickly to get a general idea of meaning or to find specific information, e.g. figures or names.

questions.question: What are the two words highlighted in the passage that describe the vital role of rivers in the development of the agriculture sector?

__
 
• The word** "watering" **indicates** that rivers provide essential water supply to the land, which is a critical factor for agriculture. **
 
• **Watering the land** ensures that crops receive **adequate moisture necessary for growth.**
 
• The term **"fertile"** suggests that **the presence of rivers contributes to the fertility of the soil.**
 
• **Fertile soil **is crucial for **the cultivation of crops because it contains the necessary nutrients for plant growth.**
 
• **Rivers **deposit silt and other minerals on the land, **enhancing the fertility of the agricultural fields.**

• **Option 4:** Countryside and villages - These terms refer to areas affected by rivers but do not describe their agricultural impact.

questions.question: Why are the rivers called natural highways?

options.text: Because they link the towns and villages
Because they avoid overflow and flood
Because national highways are built alongside their banks
Because they enrich the beauty of Bengal and Kerala

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rivers** are described **as natural highways because they facilitate transportation and connectivity. **
 
• **They serve as natural routes for moving people and goods between different locations**.
 
• Historically,** rivers have been used for navigation, enabling trade and commerce.**
 
• The passage specifically mentions that** rivers **link towns with villages, highlighting their role in connecting different parts of the country.
 
• **This connectivity provided by rivers is vital for economic development and integration of regions.**
 
• Using rivers as highways can** reduce **transportation costs and time, benefiting both rural and urban areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **Because they avoid overflow and flood - This is incorrect as the passage mentions that rivers sometimes flood the countryside, indicating they do not always avoid overflow and flood.
 
• **Option 3:** Because national highways are built alongside their banks - This is incorrect as there is no mention of national highways being built alongside river banks in the passage.
 
• **Option 4:** Because they enrich the beauty of Bengal and Kerala - This is incorrect as although rivers do enhance the beauty of these regions, the term "natural highways" specifically refers to their connectivity function.

• **Sacred: **Rivers are described as sacred, **affirming their cultural and religious significance in India,** where many rivers are worshipped and considered holy.
 
• **Huge:** The passage refers to** "huge rivers sometimes burst their banks," **pointing to the substantial size of some Indian rivers which have a significant impact on the landscape.
 
• **Small:** The passage concludes by stating** "To love India is to love her rivers, big and small,"** acknowledging the diversity in the size of rivers across India.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3:** Storable, impure, negligible - This option is incorrect as the passage does not mention rivers being storable, impure, or negligible; it highlights their positive aspects.
 
• **Option 4:** Reverse flowing, unflawed, useless - This option is incorrect because the passage does not depict rivers as reverse flowing, unflawed, or useless; on the contrary, it emphasizes their significance and benefits.
